I'm 54 years old, been farming these 8 mu in Quzhou County since I was a young man following my father around the fields. I only finished primary school, so I don't read many books, but I know this land and I watch what my neighbors do. We always do wheat-maize rotation here — that's how you make a living on the North China Plain. 

This year, I'll stick with my 8 mu of winter wheat and follow it with 8 mu of summer maize, same as always. For wheat, I planted Luyuan 502 last October — it's an improved seed that most folks in our village use, and it hasn't let me down. I rotary-tilled the soil before planting. Now that spring is here, the wheat needs care. I'll irrigate four times: once for the green-up, once at jointing, once at heading, and once during grain filling. Water from the tube well isn't cheap anymore, but Lao Wang down the road tried skipping one irrigation last year and his yield dropped badly. Better to spend the money than risk losing half the crop. For fertilizer, I'll put down about 100 jin of compound fertilizer as basal and topdress with urea at jointing — altogether that's about 17 kg of nitrogen, 7 kg of phosphorus, and 5 kg of potassium per mu. I'll spray pesticides four times: herbicide once in early spring, plus insecticide and fungicide when I see problems starting. I expect about 1000 kg per mu if the weather cooperates.

After wheat harvest in early June, I'll plant summer maize right away — the window is tight, only about a week. I'll use Denghai 605 hybrid seed; it's what everyone buys at the county supply store. I'll plant it no-tillage directly into the wheat stubble to save time and diesel. Maize needs about 19 kg nitrogen, 7 kg phosphorus, and 6 kg potassium per mu — one basal compound fertilizer application and one big urea topdress at the trumpet stage. I'll irrigate twice, and spray pesticides three times. If things go normally, I should get around 1100 kg per mu. I thought about trying cotton like some people in southern Quzhou, but cotton takes more labor and the price is uncertain. Wheat and maize give me steady food and income, and at my age I don't want to gamble.
